question.leadin: Answer the following about the Conway Cabal.
question.text: One member of the Conway Cabal, James Wilkinson, was later involved in the possibly-treasonous activities of this man, who narrowly lost to Jefferson in the 1800 presidential election and shot Alexander Hamilton in a duel.
question.clue: This politician was involved in a plot with "Number Thirteen," a Spanish agent and US Army officer named James Wilkinson, leading to this politician being tried for treason.

swap.text: This man, Harrison's running mate and vice president, succeeded him. Harrison campaigned for the presidency with the slogan "Tippecanoe and [this man] too".
swap.clue: That Secretary of State under this President negotiated a treaty that settled the border between Maine and Canada called the Webster-Ashburton Treaty.

question.leadin: This structure was initially derided as a "Folly" and a "Big Ditch," but it greatly reduced transport costs between the Atlantic Ocean and inland United States.
question.text: Name this massive engineering project built between 1817 and 1825. It allowed ships to transport goods from the Hudson River directly to the Great Lakes.
question.clue: Its construction began on July 4, 1817, and it began as a simple construction of a four-foot deep, forty-foot wide ditch.

swap.leadin: This political party's failed Presidential candidates included Charles Coteworth Pinckney and DeWitt Clinton.
swap.text: Name this early American political party, which did attain the Presidency via John Adams.
swap.clue: The Coodies were a faction of this party from Maryland.

question.leadin: Name these Speakers of the House.
question.text: This man is the only Speaker of the House to become President. This president sent Nicholas Trist to negotiate the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, which ended the Mexican War.
question.clue: During his presidency, Abraham Lincoln demanded this President show the exact location where American blood had been spilled.

swap.text: During the Second Seminole War, Native American forces were led by this man who resisted the Treaty of Payne's Landing. He died in 1838 after being captured on the orders of General Jesup.
swap.clue: Quartermaster General Thomas Jesup captured Micanopy and this man under a false white flag, after which he died in captivity of an abscess.

question.leadin: Horace Greeley's book The American Conflict was the first to claim that this politician exclaimed "John Marshall has made his decision; now let him enforce it!"
question.text: Name this president who disregarded the Supreme Court's ruling in Worcester v. Georgia. A policy enacted by this president was continued by the signing of the Treaty of New Echota under his successor.
question.clue: Chemical exposure from paint may have led Richard Lawrence to fire two pistols, both of which failed, at this man.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a time when the capital of the U.S. was captured.
swap.text: James Madison and the government were forced to flee from the British during this conflict advocated by the War Hawks and eventually settled in the Treaty of Ghent.
swap.clue: The defeat of the Guerriere by the Constitution was a significant ship action in this war, during which an attack at Beaver Dams failed due to the British being warned by Laura Secord.

question.leadin: This man was elected president in a five-way race that included such opponents as Hugh Lawson White, and he was backed early in his career by the Albany Regency and the Bucktails.
question.text: Identify this first New Yorker elected to the presidency, whose later career saw a Barnburner-backed nomination for the 1848 Free Soil ticket that helped swing the election to Zachary Taylor.
question.clue: As a state politician, this man, with the aid of such figures as future governor Silas Wright organized the Bucktails into the Albany Regency.

swap.leadin: This conflict began following the XYZ affair.
swap.text: Name this undeclared war between the U.S. and France.
swap.clue: Triumphs for that nation included the capture of the ships L'Insurgente and La Vengeance by Thomas Truxtun.

question.leadin: Name these early Supreme Court cases.
question.text: The executor of the estate of Robert Farquhar attempted to sue the state of Georgia in this 1793 case, which led to the adoption of the Eleventh Amendment.
question.clue: This first significant Supreme Court case, which ruled that the federal court had the power to hear cases in which private citizens sued states.

swap.leadin: Name these major building projects of the 19th century.
swap.text: This road, whose alternate name refers to the namesake Maryland city from which it extended to Vandalia, Illinois, was never completed, as it ran out of funding in 1839. Its construction was part of Henry Clay's American System.
swap.clue: This early federal public works project, which extended west from Maryland to Vandalia, Illinois.

question.leadin: Despite being derided as "His Accidency," John Tyler's presidency had several diplomatic accomplishments.
question.text: This treaty, partly named for a Secretary of State under John Tyler, resolved the Aroostook War, calming the border dispute between Maine and New Brunswick.
question.clue: It also outlined a border through Minnesota and the Great Lakes, cementing the Northwest Angle.

swap.leadin: This man and his brother Pierre organized themselves on the island of Barataria.
swap.text: Name this pirate. Governor William Claiborne put out an order for his capture, and later, many of his supporters and ships were captured by Commodore Daniel Patterson, but he was eventually pardoned.
swap.clue: This man, with his older brother, Pierre, met with Andrew Jackson in December 1814 and offered his assistance for a battle which ended in January the following year.

question.leadin: Herbert Storing's seven-volume collection and Morton Borden's selection of 85 of these works both include the claim that "it is very difficult to convert tyranny into freedom" from "Rhode Island is Right!"
question.text: Name this collection of works written under such pseudonyms as "Centinel," "Brutus," "The Federal Farmer," and "Cato" that took the opposite viewpoint of writings by John Jay, James Madison, and Alexander Hamilton.
question.clue: In 1965, letters by another "Farmer," thought to be Elbridge Gerry, were collected under this title alongside writings supporting the same position from the pseudonymous Brutus, Cato, and Centinel.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about money in the United States.
swap.text: In order to prevent state governors from having authority to forgive debts, Hamilton pushed for this clause to be included in the Constitution. It also prohibits states from making treaties and was used as the basis of Fletcher vs. Peck.
swap.clue: In the 1934 Blaisdell case, the Supreme Court ruled that the emergency of the Great Depression meant that Olson's moratorium on foreclosure did not violate this constitutional clause. Daniel Webster argued for the strength of this clause in Dartmouth College v. Woodward.

question.text: This governor of Pennsylvania sent the militia to stop Fries' men and arrest those who would not pay the tax; he also called out the militia during the Whiskey Rebellion.

swap.leadin: John Taliaferro likely wrote one of these documents that claimed that its subject once killed a thousand Native Americans, slept in a field of their corpses, and then ate a dozen of them for breakfast.
swap.text: Name these documents released by Philadelphia news editor John Binns during the election of 1828.
swap.answerHtml: Coffin Handbills [accept Coffin Bills; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: This pamphlets that contained vicious personal attacks accusing one candidate of consuming the corpses of defeated Native Americans while slandering his wife over the charge of alleged bigamy during the 1828 election.

question.leadin: This man's earliest solo works include the Hammerwood Lodge and the former Virginia State Penitentiary.
question.text: Name this man who was appointed surveyor of public buildings by Thomas Jefferson, in which role he put designs of American plants such as corn and tobacco in the interior of the Capitol.
question.clue: In a lull in his career, he designed a steam powered wool mill in Steubenville, Ohio as an offshoot of a partnership to build steamboats with Robert Fulton.

swap.text: Earlier, South Texas was the site of a "Cart War" in which Anglos attacked Tejano oxcarts near this city on the route between San Antonio and Indianola. On Palm Sunday, 1836, hundreds of Texan POWs were executed by firing squad in this city.
swap.answerHtml: Goliad [accept Goliad Massacre, Goliad Cart Road, or Indianola-Goliad-San Antonio Road]
swap.clue: This massacre perpetrated on James Fannin's men a month after the Battle of the Alamo. At the Battle of San Jacinto, charging soldiers cried "Remember the Alamo! Remember [this massacre]!"
